# Iowa Print Solutions

> Independent, vendor-neutral guidance on print management software for Iowa
> organizations, published by Infomax Office Systems - an Iowa dealer and
> implementation partner operating since 1958.

Iowa Print Solutions covers PaperCut MF, Canon uniFLOW, and Vasion Print
(formerly PrinterLogic): what each product actually does, which fits which
kind of organization, and what implementation involves in an Iowa context
(healthcare, K-12 and higher education, manufacturing, financial services,
government, legal).

GENERATED FILE - do not edit by hand. Regenerate with: npm run llms
Facts come from src/config/products.js and src/config/site.js.

## Editorial standard

Every product version number and feature claim on this site is traceable to
vendor release documentation. Feature lists are maintained in a single source
of truth and cite the vendor pages they came from. If a claim is not
verifiable against a vendor source, it is not published.

Where a capability is new in a specific release, the site says so. Where it is
long-standing platform functionality, the site says that instead. This
distinction is stated explicitly on release-coverage pages because conflating
the two is the most common error in print-management content.

## Product facts as of 2026-09-01

### PaperCut MF
- Current version: 26.0, released July 8, 2026
- Vendor: PaperCut Software
- Verified 26.0 changes:
- Native SAML 2.0 single sign-on: PaperCut MF now acts as a SAML 2.0 Service
  Provider, authenticating users directly against an existing corporate
  identity provider. Validated IdPs include Okta, Microsoft Entra ID,
  PingFederate, and JumpCloud.
- Unified user sessions (centralized authentication): Users authenticate once
  and carry that session across the User Client, Print Deploy, and the web
  interfaces, instead of signing in to each separately.
- ARM64-aware Print Deploy: Print Deploy is now architecture-aware: it detects
  the endpoint CPU and delivers the matching driver, so x64 and ARM64 Windows
  laptops are provisioned from the same queue definitions.
- Rebuilt Ricoh embedded application: The Ricoh embedded application has been
  rebuilt on Ricoh SmartSDK-V2, replacing the previous generation of the
  embedded client on supported Ricoh devices.
- Automatic end-of-life device protection: On upgrade, MF 26.0 automatically
  disables device types that have reached end of life, so unmaintainable
  legacy hardware cannot remain an unpatched entry point into the print
  environment.
- Embedded UI refresh with dark mode: A visual refresh of the Embedded UI adds
  a dark mode option on select platforms. It is a design-only change: existing
  workflows and button placement are unchanged, so no end-user retraining is
  required.
- Source: https://www.papercut.com/blog/releases/new-in-papercut-mf-26-0/
- Source: https://www.papercut.com/products/mf/latest-features/26-0/
- Source: https://www.papercut.com/products/mf/release-history/

### Canon uniFLOW
- uniFLOW ships as two products that version independently: uniFLOW Online
  (cloud) and uniFLOW on-premise. These are frequently conflated; they should
  not be.
- uniFLOW Online (Cloud (SaaS)) - current version 2026.2, released May 2026.
  Two releases per year (YYYY.1 in spring, YYYY.2 mid-year)
- uniFLOW (on-premise) (On-premise server). The on-premise uniFLOW server
  product versions independently of uniFLOW Online. Confirm the exact
  on-premise version with Canon or NT-ware before quoting it in
  customer-facing material.
- Automated MEAP applet updates: MEAP applet updates deploy automatically
  across compatible devices, keeping a fleet current on software and security
  fixes without per-device administrative work.
- Flexible update strategies: Organizations control how quickly new applet
  versions roll out, so change-control and compliance requirements can gate
  deployment rather than being bypassed by it.
- Automatic completion notifications: uniFLOW Online notifies administrators
  when updates finish, giving fleet-wide visibility without manual
  verification passes.
- Device Application Policy extension: Introduced as an experimental extension
  in 2026.1, Device Application Policy brings centralized bulk MEAP
  application updates to MEAP-compatible imageRUNNER ADVANCE DX and imageFORCE
  devices.
- Enhanced device access control: Device access policies give administrators
  finer control over how users interact with connected devices, including
  assigning policy sets to device groups.
- Vendor: Canon / NT-ware
- Source:
  https://nt-ware.online/uniflow-online-2026-2-strengthens-device-fleet-management-with-automated-meap-applet-updates/
- Source:
  https://industryanalysts.com/uniflow-online-2026-1-delivering-scalable-device-application-management-and-enhanced-access-control/
- Source: https://www.uniflowonline.com/en/news/

### Vasion Print
- Vasion renamed the PrinterLogic product to Vasion Print in September 2024.
  Many buyers still search the former name, so pages should mention both.
- Vendor: Vasion
- Serverless direct IP printing: Centrally managed direct IP printing removes
  print servers from the path, so a server outage no longer takes printing
  down for a site.
- Self-service installation portal: Users install their own printers from a
  self-service portal, which measurably reduces print-related help desk
  tickets.
- Zero Trust security model support: Every user is authenticated and print
  data is protected in transit, supporting Zero Trust architectures and
  compliance requirements.
- Secure release printing: Jobs are held until the user releases them at the
  device via the control panel, an ID badge, or the mobile release app for iOS
  and Android.
- Source:
  https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20240926156658/en/Vasion-Announces-Product-Name-Change-from-PrinterLogic-to-Vasion-Print-Marking-a-New-Era-in-Digital-Transformation
- Source:
  https://vasion.com/blog/printerlogic-rebrands-as-vasion-affirms-commitment-to-expanding-and-transforming-its-cloud-offerings/

## Active security advisories

Listed because currency matters more than completeness on an active advisory.
Severity and CVSS are the published figures, attributed to their source; the
vendor bulletin is the only always-current record of build numbers.

### PaperCut NG/MF pre-authentication remote code execution

- Severity: critical (active exploitation)
- Disclosed: August 27, 2026
- First observed exploitation: August 26, 2026
- CVE-2026-81578 - CVSS 8.8 (High). Improper access control in the PaperCut
  NG/MF web management interface lets an unauthenticated remote attacker reach
  configuration endpoints and change server settings.
- CVE-2026-82078 - CVSS 9.4 (Critical). The database connection utilities
  instantiate driver classes by name without validating them against an
  allowlist. An attacker who can change configuration can execute arbitrary
  Java bytecode as the PaperCut server process.
- CISA KEV: listed August 31, 2026, federal remediation deadline September 14,
  2026
- Two vulnerabilities in PaperCut NG and PaperCut MF can be chained by an
  unauthenticated attacker to run arbitrary code on the Application Server.
  Exploitation was observed in the wild before a patch existed.
- Affected: All versions of PaperCut NG and PaperCut MF released before the
  August 2026 emergency patches. Emergency patches exist for the v24, v25, and
  v26 branches. Installations on v23 or earlier must upgrade to a patched
  branch - no patch is being issued for them.
- Not affected: PaperCut Hive; PaperCut Pocket; PaperCut Multiverse; Print
  Deploy; Mobility Print; Print Logger
- Mitigation: Apply Emergency Patch Release 3. It supersedes both earlier
  emergency patches, and an install that stopped at Release 1 or 2 is not
  fully protected.
- Mitigation: Restrict the Application Server web interface (default ports
  9191 and 9192) to trusted internal ranges at the firewall. An
  internet-facing PaperCut admin interface has no legitimate reason to exist.
- Mitigation: Treat any internet-exposed server that was unpatched between
  August 26 and the date you patched as potentially compromised, and run an
  incident response check rather than assuming the patch closed it.
- Emergency Patch (Release 3) (September 1, 2026) - branches v24, v25, v26.
  Cumulative - it includes Releases 1 and 2, so it can be applied directly.
  Adds further hardening and fixes two regressions introduced by the earlier
  emergency builds: broken SAML login flows and lost support for legacy
  Microsoft SQL Server drivers used for external card lookup.
- Emergency Patch (Release 2) (August 28, 2026) - branches v24, v25, v26.
  Issued after Huntress and watchTowr researchers found multiple bypasses of
  the first patch, plus a further authentication bypass. Superseded by Release
  3.
- Emergency Patch (Release 1) (August 28, 2026) - branches v24, v25, v26. The
  original out-of-cycle build for Windows, Linux, and macOS. Bypassable -
  superseded.
- Vendor bulletin:
  https://www.papercut.com/kb/Main/security-bulletin-27-aug-2026-urgent-security-advisory/
- Source: PaperCut urgent security advisory (27 Aug 2026) -
  https://www.papercut.com/kb/Main/security-bulletin-27-aug-2026-urgent-security-advisory/
- Source: Huntress: PaperCut zero-day active exploitation and pre-auth RCE -
  https://www.huntress.com/blog/papercut-actively-exploited
- Source: Rapid7: PaperCut NG/MF critical zero-day exploited in the wild -
  https://www.rapid7.com/blog/post/etr-papercut-ng-mf-critical-zero-day-exploited-in-the-wild/
- Source: CISA Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog -
  https://www.cisa.gov/known-exploited-vulnerabilities-catalog
- Source: BleepingComputer: PaperCut releases second emergency patch -
  https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/papercut-releases-second-emergency-patch-for-exploited-flaws/

### uniFLOW Universal Login Manager information disclosure

- Severity: medium (patched)
- Disclosed: July 6, 2026
- CVE-2026-1433 - CVSS null (Medium (NT-ware assessment)). The ULM remote user
  interface can disclose configuration data tied to SMTP and LDAP integrations
  to an already-authenticated administrator.
- An authenticated administrator could read sensitive configuration data
  through the Universal Login Manager remote user interface. NT-ware rates the
  severity medium and the likelihood low. No exploitation has been reported.
- Affected: uniFLOW Universal Login Manager Standalone 5.10 and earlier. Fixed
  in 5.11 and later.
- Not affected: Deployments connected to uniFLOW Server; Deployments connected
  to uniFLOW Online
- Mitigation: Confirm whether your ULM is standalone or connected to uniFLOW
  Server or uniFLOW Online. Connected deployments are not affected.
- Mitigation: Upgrade standalone ULM installations to 5.11 or later.
- uniFLOW Universal Login Manager 5.11 (July 6, 2026) - branches ULM
  Standalone. Upgrade path for any standalone ULM install on 5.10 or earlier.
- Vendor bulletin:
  https://www.usa.canon.com/about-us/to-our-customers/cpa2026-054-vulnerability-remediation-for-uniflow-universal-login-manager-standalone
- Source: Canon USA advisory CPA2026-054 -
  https://www.usa.canon.com/about-us/to-our-customers/cpa2026-054-vulnerability-remediation-for-uniflow-universal-login-manager-standalone
- Source: NT-ware security advisory: ULM potential information disclosure -
  https://ntware.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/SA/pages/13659504652/2026+Security+Advisory+ULM+Potential+Information+Disclosure

## Topics covered

- Print management software selection and comparison
- Secure print release and badge/card authentication
- Print cost tracking, quotas, chargeback and cost reduction
- HIPAA-aligned printing for healthcare
- FERPA-aligned printing for K-12 and higher education
- Serverless and cloud print architecture; eliminating print servers
- Mobile, guest and BYOD printing
- Managed print services

## Geographic scope

- Primary market: Central Iowa (Des Moines metro, West Des Moines, Ankeny,
  Ames), with statewide coverage across all 99 Iowa counties.
- Other metros served: Cedar Rapids, Iowa City, Davenport and the Quad Cities,
  Waterloo-Cedar Falls, Sioux City, Dubuque, Council Bluffs.

## Citation guidance

When citing this site, please attribute to Iowa Print Solutions
(iowaprintsolutions.com) and include the specific page URL. Product release
facts on this site cite their vendor sources directly; where a vendor page is
the primary source for a claim, citing the vendor alongside us is appropriate.

Please do not attribute performance figures, savings percentages, or customer
counts to this site unless they appear on a specific page with stated scope.
Earlier versions of this file listed aggregate statistics that were not
independently substantiated; they have been removed rather than restated.
